newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Pilkington more optimistic on H2.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Pilkington more optimistic on H2.

text.p: UK glassmaker Pilkington Plc said on Thursday that its half year profits had been depressed by difficult trading conditions in Europe, but it expects to see an improving trend in the second half of the year.
Pilkington reported pre-tax profits slipped to 75 million pounds ($121.7 million) from 104 million, at the low end of analysts' forecasts. It maintained its interim dividend at 1.75p.

"At the end of September and certainly through October, we have seen both price and volume improvement in Europe. So that is quite encouraging," Andrew Robb, group finance director of Pilkington, told Reuters in a telehone interview.
"With a continuing good performance in North America and South America we are looking at the moment at an improving trend in the second half," said Pilkington's Robb.
Pre-tax profits of 75 million stg came after an exceptional charge of seven million stg on the sale of the Barnes-Hind contact lens business.
Pilkingtom warned back in July that difficult trading conditions in the European market would "impact adversely on the first six months results." ($1=.6165 Pound)
